newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria stops British flights into the country.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria stops British flights into the country.

text.p: Nigeria on Friday stopped British aircraft from landing in the African country, airline officials and diplomats said.

"A letter was sent to the (British) Department of Trade that with immediate effect British-registered aircraft cannot land in Nigeria and so we have had to cancel our flight to Lagos today," a British Airways official told Reuters.
The action appeared to be in retaliation for the British government barring Nigeria Airways planes some two months ago.

"The British government action against Nigeria Airways was taken for safety reasons," said a British diplomat, adding "There is no basis for recriminations and we are certain the matter will be resolved soon."
The Lagos-London route is a lucrative one for British Airways, which operates daily filghts to and from Nigeria.
"This action is going to be very disruptive both for Nigerian passengers and foreigners," said one travel agent.

Cash-strapped Nigeria Airways has suffered a string of problems recently, including the suspension of its insurance cover by state-owned National Insurance Corporation of Nigeria (NICON) for several weeks.
This was restored this week when Nigeria Airways was due to resume its international flights, including the London route.
Nigerian sources said the British government decided that planes of the Nigerian national carrier could not land in Britain but that it could operate flights to London using leased aircraft.
Relations between Nigeria and its former colonial power Britain have been stormy since 1993 when a presidential election to restore democracy in Nigeria was annulled.
Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth, which groups Britain and its former colonies, in 1995 when it hanged nine minority rights activists in defiance of world opinion.

The Abuja government on Thursday told the new British government not to do anything to damage their mutual relations following remarks by foreign secretary Robin Cook that Britain would support sanctions against Nigeria to push it to restore democracy and respect human rights.
